source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Keep unopened insulin in a household freezer until the day it is first used, then thaw it at room temperature.","B":"Keep unopened insulin refrigerated at the manufacturer-recommended temperature and never freeze it; room-temperature limits vary by product.","C":"Store unopened insulin at room temperature indefinitely because refrigeration is unnecessary before the first dose.","D":"Keep insulin next to a warm appliance or sunny window so the solution remains near body temperature before injection."}}
source_row.rationale: FDA states that unopened insulin should be refrigerated at approximately 36°F to 46°F when possible, should not be frozen, and that room-temperature stability varies by product and conditions.
